newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh on high alert as cyclonic storm nears.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh on high alert as cyclonic storm nears.

text.p: Some 25,000 police and civil volunteers were on standby in Bangladesh on Sunday for emergency evacuation and relief operations as a cyclonic storm approached the coast, disaster management officials said.
They said volunteers using megaphones were warning people on the coast and offshore islands of the impending danger as the storm progressed from the Bay of Bengal.
Residents were advised to move to cyclone shelters or elsewhere for safety.
Police have been asked to ensure that boats were ready to ferry people from the islands to the shore, one official in Chittagong told Reuters.
"We are doing everything possible on our part," he said.
Weather officials said the storm was 600 km (370 miles) from Chittagong port on Sunday afternoon and might hit the shore early on Monday at more than 150 kph (90 mph).
Officials in the coastal district of Cox's Bazar said more than 3,000 fishing boats were still far into the Bay.
"Most of the boats have radio and we hope they could rush to safety before it is too late," one official said.
The storm could trigger waves up to 12 feet (four metres) high, meteorological officials said.
Chittagong's port authority has asked all ships to move to outer anchorage to minimise damage from collision in case the storm hits.
"We are taking all precautions although we still hope the cyclone will pass Bangladesh coast towards Burma's Akyab province," one port official said.
Officials at Mongla port said they were taking "maximum precautions for a possible onslaught."
"Adequate warnings have been issued to all concerned, including ships' pilots and port operators. The storm may hit us next morning," one offical told reporters in nearby Khulna town.
All fishing boats and trawlers in the northern part of the Bay of Bengal have been advised to remain close to the coast and take shelter.
A similar storm early last month devastated the Andhra Pradesh coast, killing 971 people.
Bangladesh's worst cyclone in 1991 killed more than 138,000 people and left millions homeless.
